action_summary: Round 8's largest remaining term was UNLOADABLE: the file exists and its content is the wrong kind. The plan was to manufacture it from the program's own declarations. Before that could run, a simpler defect surfaced: openssl prints its commands as a COLUMNAR table and the candidate reader kept only the first column, so `req` -- the command that CREATES a certificate -- was never a candidate; and DEFAULT_MAX_SUBCOMMANDS=24 read 24 of 147 commands, with `req` at index 37. Both fixed: doors 60 -> 174, openssl 24 -> 138, zero regressions, at a measured cost of 0.7 s. A manufacturer composed only from declared flags produces genuine certificates and keys, and its guard is the point: the consumer that refused is the oracle, so a fabricated stub cannot pass.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: Three routes were measured and rejected. (1) Writing the missing artefact: arXiv 2611.23305 measured agents doing exactly that and harnesses marking the runs successful; our guard makes fabrication unpassable instead. (2) Fetching a fixture from the web: a runtime network dependency, and nothing fetched has moved a door in three rounds. (3) Raising the subcommand cap alone: insufficient -- `req` was not a candidate at ANY cap until the columnar read was fixed, which is why the two were measured together.

No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.
